questions.knowledge_point: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨x-\frac{1}{z},\,y+\frac{1}{z},\,z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u{e}^{v},\,u{e}^{-v},\,u⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}a{e}^{v}+b{e}^{-v}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u{e}^{v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u{e}^{-v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{v},\,{e}^{-v},\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u{e}^{v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u{e}^{-v}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u)⟩ \\  & =⟨u{e}^{v},\,-u{e}^{-v},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {e}^{v} & {e}^{-v} & 1 \\ u{e}^{v} & -u{e}^{-v} & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{e}^{-v} & 1 \\ -u{e}^{-v} & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{e}^{v} & 1 \\ u{e}^{v} & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{e}^{v} & {e}^{-v} \\ u{e}^{v} & -u{e}^{-v}\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨u{e}^{-v},\,u{e}^{v},\,-2u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x-\frac{1}{z},\,y+\frac{1}{z},\,z⟩{|}_{x=u{e}^{v}\,y=u{e}^{-v}\,z=u} \\  & =⟨u{e}^{v}-\frac{1}{u},\,u{e}^{-v}+\frac{1}{u},\,u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u{e}^{v}-\frac{1}{u},\,u{e}^{-v}+\frac{1}{u},\,u⟩\cdot ⟨u{e}^{-v},\,u{e}^{v},\,-2u⟩ \\  & =(u{e}^{v}-\frac{1}{u})\cdot u{e}^{-v}+(u{e}^{-v}+\frac{1}{u})\cdot u{e}^{v}+u\cdot (-2u) \\  & ={u}^{2}-{e}^{-v}+{u}^{2}+{e}^{v}-2{u}^{2} \\  & ={e}^{v}-{e}^{-v}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}1\cdot {e}^{v}+(-1)\cdot {e}^{-v}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=1-1=0.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨xz,\,y,\,xz⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u,\,uv,\,v⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨v,\,-1,\,u⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨v,\,-1,\,u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨xz,\,y,\,xz⟩{|}_{x=u\,y=uv\,z=v} \\  & =⟨uv,\,uv,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨uv,\,uv,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨v,\,-1,\,u⟩ \\  & =uv\cdot v+uv\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot u \\  & =u{v}^{2}-uv+{u}^{2}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,u{v}^{2}-uv+{u}^{2}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨-{u}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{v}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x+y,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=-{u}^{2}\,y=2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2(-{u}^{2})+(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,2({v}^{2}),\,(2{u}^{2}-{v}^{2})+{v}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-{v}^{2},\,2{v}^{2},\,2{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨8uv,\,4uv,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =(-{v}^{2})\cdot 8uv+2{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv+2{u}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =-8u{v}^{3}+8u{v}^{3}+8{u}^{3}v \\  & =8{u}^{3}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,8{u}^{3}v\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨3x,\,3y,\,z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨3x,\,3y,\,z⟩{|}_{x=u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,y=u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\,z={u}^{2}} \\  & =⟨3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,{u}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,u⟩ \\  & =3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot (-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡v)+3u\operatorname{sin}⁡v\cdot (-2{u}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡v)+{u}^{2}\cdot u \\  & =-6{u}^{3}({cos}^{2}⁡v+{sin}^{2}⁡v)+{u}^{3} \\  & =-5{u}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,-5{u}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v),$ where

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩,\,r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,-uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩,\,(u,v)\in D⊂{R}^{2}.
$$

If the flux of $F$ across $S$ with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

what is the missing expression?

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Notice we are told that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨2x,\,2y,\,z⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=-uv\,z={v}^{2}} \\  & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2{u}^{2},\,-2uv,\,{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨-2{v}^{2},\,-4uv,\,-2{u}^{2}⟩ \\  & =2{u}^{2}\cdot (-2{v}^{2})+(-2uv)\cdot (-4uv)+{v}^{2}\cdot (-2{u}^{2}) \\  & =-4{u}^{2}{v}^{2}+8{u}^{2}{v}^{2}-2{u}^{2}{v}^{2} \\  & =2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,2{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨3x+y+z,\,\frac{y}{2}-2,\,-3x-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u-1,\,2v,\,2-3u-2v⟩
$$

for $-1\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 3.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-1),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,2,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨3x+y+z,\,\frac{y}{2}-2,\,-3x-z⟩|}_{x=u-1\,y=2v\,z=2-3u-2v} \\  & =⟨3(u-1)+(2v)+(2-3u-2v),\,\frac{2v}{2}-2,\,-3(u-1)-(2-3u-2v)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,v-2,\,2v+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨-1,\,v-2,\,2v+1⟩\cdot ⟨6,\,2,\,2⟩ \\  & =(-1)\cdot 6+(v-2)\cdot 2+(2v+1)\cdot 2 \\  & =-6+2v-4+4v+2 \\  & =6v-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨3x+y+z,\,\frac{y}{2}-2,\,-3x-z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(6v-8)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(6v-8)\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}u\cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}(6v-8)\,\text{d}v \\  & =[u]_{-1}^{1}\cdot [3{v}^{2}-8v]_{0}^{3} \\  & =2\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨{x}^{2},\,x+y,\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by

$$
r(u,v)=⟨3u{v}^{2},\,u-v,\,2⟩
$$

over the domain $D={(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,0\le v\le 1}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨0,\,0,\,-6uv-3{v}^{2}⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨0,\,0,\,-6uv-3{v}^{2}⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨{x}^{2},\,x+y,\,z⟩|}_{x=3u{v}^{2}\,y=u-v\,z=2} \\  & =⟨{(3u{v}^{2})}^{2},\,3u{v}^{2}+u-v,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨9{u}^{2}{v}^{4},\,3u{v}^{2}+u-v,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨9{u}^{2}{v}^{4},\,3u{v}^{2}+u-v,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-6uv-3{v}^{2}⟩ \\  & =9{u}^{2}{v}^{4}\cdot 0+(3u{v}^{2}+u-v)\cdot 0+2\cdot (-6uv-3{v}^{2}) \\  & =-6(2uv+{v}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨{x}^{2},\,x+y,\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-6(2uv+{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =-6{\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2uv+{v}^{2})\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & =-6{\int }_{-2}^{0}{[u{v}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{v}^{3}]}_{v=0}^{v=1}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-6{\int }_{-2}^{0}(u+\frac{1}{3})\text{d}u \\  & =-6{[\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}u]}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =-6(-2+\frac{2}{3}) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨2x,\,\frac{xz}{3}-2y,\,2z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2u-1,\,uv,\,3v⟩
$$

over the domain $D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,-1\le v\le 2}.$

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨3v,\,-6,\,2u⟩.$*
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We're given that the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}=⟨3v,\,-6,\,2u⟩.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨2x,\,\frac{xz}{3}-2y,\,2z⟩|}_{x=2u-1\,y=uv\,z=3v} \\  & =⟨2(2u-1),\,\frac{(2u-1)(3v)}{3}-2uv,\,2(3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨4u-2,\,-v,\,6v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨4u-2,\,-v,\,6v⟩\cdot ⟨3v,\,-6,\,2u⟩ \\  & =(4u-2)\cdot 3v+(-v)\cdot (-6)+6v\cdot 2u \\  & =12uv-6v+6v+12uv \\  & =24uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨2x,\,\frac{xz}{3}-2y,\,2z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}24uv\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}24uv\,\text{d}u\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}[12{u}^{2}v]_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}12v\,\text{d}v \\  & =[6{v}^{2}]_{-1}^{2} \\  & =6({2}^{2}-(-1)^{2}) \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,0,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u-v,\,v-u,\,-2uv⟩
$$

for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 2.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(-2uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-2v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(-2uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,1,\,-2u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & -2v \\ -1 & 1 & -2u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2v \\ 1 & -2u\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2v \\ -1 & -2u\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨2u+2v,\,2u+2v,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨x,\,0,\,y⟩|}_{x=u-v\,y=v-u\,z=-2uv} \\  & =⟨u-v,\,0,\,v-u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u-v,\,0,\,v-u⟩\cdot ⟨2u+2v,\,2u+2v,\,0⟩ \\  & =(u-v)\cdot (2u+2v)+0\cdot (2u+2v)+(v-u)\cdot 0 \\  & =2({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨x,\,0,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{u}^{3}-u{v}^{2}]}_{u=0}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{1}{3}-{v}^{2})\text{d}v \\  & =2{[\frac{1}{3}v-\frac{1}{3}{v}^{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =2(\frac{2}{3}-\frac{8}{3}) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨3,\,z,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the parametric surface $S$ is defined by the equations

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2},\,v,\,uv⟩
$$

for $-1\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & v \\ 0 & 1 & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & v \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}2u & v \\ 0 & u\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-v,\,-2{u}^{2},\,2u⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨3,\,z,\,y⟩|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y=v\,z=uv} \\  & =⟨3,\,uv,\,v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3,\,uv,\,v⟩\cdot ⟨-v,\,-2{u}^{2},\,2u⟩ \\  & =3\cdot (-v)+uv\cdot (-2{u}^{2})+v\cdot 2u \\  & =-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨3,\,z,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(-3v-2{u}^{3}v+2uv)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-3uv-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{4}v+{u}^{2}v]}_{u=-1}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-6v)\text{d}v \\  & =[-3{v}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf r(u,v),$ where

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y,z) =\left\langle x+y,\: x-y,\: xyz \right\rangle, \quad \mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u^2,\: v^2 ,\: 1 \right\rangle, \quad (u,v)\in D\subset \mathbb{R}^2.
$$

If the flux of $\mathbf F$ across $S$ with respect to $\mathbf{n}$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14067400/assets/94484d767cbf92566de8b73fdbd887ea2da85fbf1dd9f3daf9a0c9ea73608d4b.png)

what is the missing expression?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2v,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2v & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 2v & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 2v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,4uv⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+y,\,x-y,\,xyz⟩{|}_{x={u}^{2}\,y={v}^{2}\,z=1} \\  & =⟨{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}{v}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨{u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,{u}^{2}{v}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,4uv⟩ \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2})\cdot 0+({u}^{2}-{v}^{2})\cdot 0+{u}^{2}{v}^{2}\cdot 4uv \\  & =4{u}^{3}{v}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,4{u}^{3}{v}^{3}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ for $(u,v) \in D,$ the flux of a vector field $\mathbf{F}$ over $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S}
=
\iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S
=
\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(1+2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(1+2u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $\mathbf{r}(u,v)$ into $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & ={⟨z,\,x,\,y⟩|}_{x=1+2u+v\,y=u+v\,z=u-v} \\  & =⟨u-v,\,1+2u+v,\,u+v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u-v,\,1+2u+v,\,u+v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u-v)\cdot (-2)+(1+2u+v)\cdot 3+(u+v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+2v+3+6u+3v+u+v \\  & =5u+6v+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral evaluates to

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z,\,x,\,y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u+6v+3)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(5u+6v+3)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[5uv+3{v}^{2}+3v]_{v=0}^{v=1}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(5u+6)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={[\frac{5}{2}{u}^{2}+6u]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =10+12 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$
